source: CoreGuard Quilla Cyber Codex (original educational summaries; cites public frameworks)

entries.title: Mobile phishing & smishing
entries.summary: Fraudulent messages push you to malicious apps or credential pages.
entries.body: Smishing uses SMS/RCS; phishing uses email/chat. Deep links can open attacker-controlled app routes. Urgency + brand impersonation are hallmarks. Verify via official apps/bookmarks, not message links.
entries.defense: Don't install APKs from messages. Scan new apps. Enable Shield for known-bad domains.

entries.title: Android banking trojans & overlays
entries.summary: Malware that steals credentials via overlays or Accessibility abuse.
entries.body: Trojans may request Accessibility to read screens or draw overlays over banking apps. They often arrive via sideload or fake stores. Unusual Accessibility prompts are a red flag.
entries.defense: Audit Accessibility services; remove unknown ones; rescan.

entries.title: Mobile supply-chain & SDK risk
entries.summary: Hostile or sloppy third-party code ships inside otherwise legit apps.
entries.body: SDKs can exfiltrate data or introduce vulnerabilities. Typosquat packages trick developers. Maintain inventories, prefer maintained libraries, and watch privacy policies for surprising data flows.
entries.defense: Review CoreGuard supply-chain tooling when available; minimize unnecessary apps.

entries.title: OWASP Mobile Top 10 (orientation)
entries.summary: Common mobile risk themes used in industry conversations.
entries.body: Themes typically include improper credential usage, inadequate supply-chain security, insecure authentication/authorization, insufficient input/output validation, insecure communication, inadequate privacy controls, insecure GUI, security misconfiguration, insecure data storage, and insufficient cryptography — exact labels evolve; MASVS is the durable control map.
entries.defense: Use MASVS categories in Compliance rather than chasing Top-10 mnemonics alone.
